clue.text: The exterior part of Brazil, say?

definitions.meaning: the outer casing of something, read literally as a hard protective covering
not the country but the brazil, a large three-sided nut

explanation.surface: A geography question about the outer regions of the South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil looks like the country; it is the brazil nut, whose outer casing is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard outer casing of a brazil, or any other nut, is its shell.

clue.text: Devise no reforms for drastic decline

indicators.note: the letters are formed again into a different shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to abandon reform plans that could bring about economic collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a sudden steep fall, used figuratively for prices or fortunes plunging.

clue.text: Colloquially speaking, it isn't corruption

definitions.meaning: first meaning: '..., a dialect contraction of it ain't
second meaning: a contaminating trace or moral stain

explanation.walkthrough: The surface denies that something is corrupt; the informal contraction 'tain't, for 'it ain't', supplies one sense, without its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or decay, a form of corruption.

clue.text: What about new supermarket where chicken's kept?

indicators.note: turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: eh? is a request to repeat, like what?
the Co-op is a British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a new supermarket has a place for keeping poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British grocery and supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen-coop is a small cage or pen in which a hen or other poultry is kept.

clue.text: Leader of Labour Party catching United game

indicators.note: the leading letter and the party word together catch hold of the letter, taking it inside
the leader is the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Labour leader at a celebration watching a Manchester United match.
explanation.walkthrough: A do is British informal for a party; U for United, as in football club names.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game in which counters race round according to dice throws.

clue.text: French writer in drunken stupor

indicators.note: someone drunken staggers about, so the letters of the next word reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French author found slumped in an alcoholic haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was the French novelist who wrote In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Stand in for salesman with frilly material

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
lace is a delicate openwork fabric used for frills

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman substituting for a colleague, armed with frilly samples.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace someone is to take their place, standing in as a substitute.

clue.text: Draw out sun's heat, heating houses

indicators.note: the words contain the answer the way a house holds its occupants

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to harness solar warmth for domestic heating systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like a noun for homes; it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe is to draw a blade out of its scabbard.

clue.text: Barbie, say, books a car

parts.note: the Barbie doll is an example of a toy
OT, the Old Testament books of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: Barbie the doll reserving a hire car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like a verb meaning reserves; it is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Toyota is the Japanese manufacturer, and its name stands for one of its cars.

clue.text: Reveal everything, in the main?

definitions.meaning: to tell all, but literally to bare the whole body
usually 'mostly', but the main is an old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but the main is the sea, and baring everything in it is a nude swim.
explanation.definitionFit: A swim taken with no clothes on, typically in the sea or a lake, bares the swimmer completely.

clue.text: I swerve off after parking trailers

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: the letters go off course, out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver veering away after pulling up in a car park while towing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailers' looks like towed vehicles; it means film advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: Previews are short extracts shown in advance to advertise a forthcoming film, also called trailers.

clue.text: Troublesome sports broadcaster

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school sports
Sky is the British satellite television company

explanation.surface: A grumble about an irritating television sports channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster; PE (physical education) is sports lessons at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pesky is annoying and causes nuisance, so it is a synonym for troublesome.

clue.text: Dorothy, Charlie, Oscar and Mike's business

parts.note: Dot is the short form of the name Dorothy
C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Four friends who jointly own a small company.
explanation.walkthrough: Three of the names are NATO alphabet code words, each giving its initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotcom is a company that trades over the internet, a type of business.

clue.text: E.g. Mo Salah on the ball, warning of an attack

parts.note: Salah plays for Liverpool, whose players are nicknamed the Reds
being on the ball means being quick and watchful

explanation.surface: A football commentator noting that the striker in possession is about to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Salah is a Liverpool footballer; Liverpool play in red and are called the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is the highest state of readiness, signalling danger or attack is imminent.

clue.text: What player does after a let in tennis books

definitions.text: What player does after a let in tennis

explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed, so the server serves again; split, the answer reads that way.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a table or seat is to book it, so reserves means books.

clue.text: Sin here blocked by one Democrat — Ms Harris?

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or sin

indicators.note: the word for here is obstructed by the letters placed in its middle

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A political jibe at the American Democrat Kamala Harris as sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamala Harris served as deputy to President Biden, so she is an example of the role; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Minder, guy accompanying Queen Elizabeth I

parts.note: a chap is a man or fellow
ER, Elizabeth Regina, her royal cipher
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bodyguard escorting the Tudor monarch Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elizabeth I' looks like one monarch; the I is split off to give one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone supervises and protects a young person, a kind of minder.

clue.text: Great admirer of irate old rogue

indicators.note: rogue as in out of control, letters gone astray from their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A devoted fan of an angry elderly scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, and loosely is someone who reveres a person excessively.

clue.text: Doctor Watson needs it, having no idea what to do

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dr Watson, Sherlock Holmes's baffled companion, needs help because he is stumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like Watson's title, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at one's wits' end is an idiom for being so perplexed you cannot think what to try next.

clue.text: One can't fly east from Germany with lots of cash

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A grounded traveller heading east from Germany with plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird, one that cannot fly.

clue.text: Conned Edward, nursing neck pain

indicators.note: holding something close, so the name wraps around the pain

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
a rick is a sprain or wrench, as of the neck

explanation.surface: Edward, swindled while suffering a stiff neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricked means deceived or fooled, a synonym for conned.

clue.text: Rascals, oddly, such as those in the House of Commons

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: those in the House of Commons
parts.note: MPs, Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: A jibe that British parliamentarians are a bunch of rogues behaving strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' reads as strangely; it picks the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scamps are mischievous people, especially children, much like rascals.

clue.text: Showing imagination etc, I rave frenziedly

indicators.note: doing something frenziedly means wildly and chaotically, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of their inventiveness while ranting wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative is an adjective for being inventive and original, using imagination.

clue.text: Banish Charles's bride with a lot of charm

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, married Prince Charles; Di is her short name

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a spell is a magic charm

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about Princess Diana banishing gloom with her charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Di was Princess Diana, Charles's first wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or scatter, a synonym for banish.

clue.text: Still baking inside Post Office

indicators.note: this word goes into the middle of the office abbreviation

parts.note: baking hot, very hot

explanation.surface: A post office that remains sweltering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb; it is the noun for a single photograph, as from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single static photograph, especially one taken from a film.

clue.text: Asian desert, one with marsh to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a bog is a marsh
the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Geography of a desert with a wetland on its northern edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Kiwi eaten by grandma or in-laws

indicators.note: the answer is swallowed up inside these words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kiwi fruit consumed by a family member at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwi looks like the fruit; it is the nickname for a New Zealander.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maori is a member of New Zealand's indigenous people, and Kiwi is slang for any New Zealander.

clue.text: What wine sellers may do somewhere near Manchester

definitions.meaning: first meaning: keep the fortified wine in stock, read as two words
second meaning: a town in Greater Manchester

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words it describes a wine merchant's inventory; whole, it is a town southeast of Manchester in northwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockport is a large town in Greater Manchester, close to the city itself.

clue.text: Look at article and become furious

parts.note: to see something is to look at it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone reads a newspaper piece and is enraged by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical word.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil inwardly with anger, being furious without showing it fully.

clue.text: We hear Irish playwright tolerated a swine

indicators.note: the words are spoken, so the playwright and the verb make the answer's sound

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Dublin-born dramatist
bore, as in endured

explanation.surface: Gossip that Oscar Wilde put up with a boorish acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild boar is a wild pig, a member of the swine family.
